title: Bank of England's existing East India Company loan
description: An archive catalogue identifies a note about prolongation of an existing £50,000 loan. The document does not establish new funds advanced on March 20.

title: Government loan to relieve the East India Company
description: An 1813 Commons historical account describes a £1.4 million government loan arranged after the Company's 1773 appeal. Parliamentary history confirms enabling legislation; the specific installments and original receipts are not yet checked.

title: Prospective commission for Hutchinson sons' tea-consignee firm
description: Massachusetts Commonwealth Museum reports a 6% sales commission for the two sons' tea consignment. It would apply to completed sales, not automatically to the value of all tea shipped. No payment to the sons or their father has been verified.

title: Joshua Winslow anticipates commission from tea sales
description: Winslow's November 18 private letter says a 'handsome commission' could be earned if the tea scheme worked. It states no monetary amount, rate, or completed disbursement.

title: Bank of England's original loan to the Crown
description: Original Bank subscribers raised £1.2m, which the Bank lent to government to support war against France. Annual interest of 8% was secured by Tonnage and Excise taxes. Not a personal payment to William III.

title: £2 million East India trade-access public borrowing scheme
description: British Library describes the £2m public borrowing arrangement tied to trade privileges and the incorporation of new East India companies. This figure describes the borrowing/subscription scheme, not a verified list of installments received by the Crown.

title: Old East India Company's stake in the rival English Company
description: The British Library records a £315k stake held by the old East India Company via its treasurer. The amount is a financial interest, not proof that £315k changed hands on a single date.

title: Proposed £4.2m Bank–South Sea restructuring arrangement
description: A circa-1722 Bank archive item describes proposals for a £4.2m payment and a separate October 1722 document records an agreement to purchase South Sea Company stock. Neither catalogue entry alone verifies that the full sum was paid as cash on a specified date.

title: Engraftment Act: proposed South Sea debt transfer NOT executed
description: Engraftment legislation received royal assent on 23 March 1721, but according to archival scholarship neither Bank of England nor East India Company actually assumed South Sea Company debt under this plan. No principal or cash flow is asserted; later 1722 arrangements are separate.
